entry.title: The Missing Feature Every AI Assistant Needs: Transparent Usage Indicators
entry.summary:
Overview:
This article examines why transparent usage indicators should be a fundamental part of modern AI assistants and digital services. Keywords: Artificial intelligence (AI), AI assistants, user experience (UX), user interface (UI), usage limits, usage quotas, usage meters, usage indicators, usage tracking, rate limits, throttling, resource allocation, feature availability, usage transparency, product design, human-computer interaction (HCI), customer experience (CX), user expectations, digital trust, product usability, subscription services, and responsible AI design. Transparent usage indicators should be a standard part of every AI experience. Whether we're generating images, analyzing files, using advanced models, conducting research, or accessing other features, users deserve to know where they stand. A little transparency goes a long way toward building trust in a product. I think there are at least four things AI assistants need to do a much better job of: A visible usage meter: Show users how much of their available usage remains, rather than making them guess.
Advance warnings: Notify users when they're approaching a usage limit, not just after they've exceeded it.
A clear reset countdown: Tell users exactly when their usage will become available again, preferably before they run into a restriction.
Feature-specific usage information: Clearly explain which limits apply to which features, so users understand what they can still do when one limit is reached.
AI tools should empower users, not leave them guessing about when their access might suddenly disappear. Can you think of anything else that should be included? Let me know in the comments!

entry.title: How to Set, Toggle, and Retrieve Node.js Feature Flags via REST API (Rollback First)
entry.summary: How to Set, Toggle, and Retrieve Node.js Feature Flags via REST API (Rollback First) Short answer: retrieve a revisioned flag before each scheduled import, set it with a reason, toggle it only with a conditional write, and fail closed when the REST response is unavailable. For a fintech import, that makes rollback safer than changing code while zero-result evidence is still being investigated. A feature flag for a scheduled financial import should be a rollback control, not a remote light switch. Keep the decision local to the worker, record it with the import run, and fail closed when the response is missing or malformed.
